messages:
Simon (Customer): hey team — we just saw a response from our VPC endpoint (prod-712) that included a different tenant's model_id and a short snippet of another customer's prompt. not PII afaict but definitely wrong. happened twice in ~8m. can someone confirm? logs attached: 

Simon (Customer): ```
resp(2026-03-15T09:12:03Z) {
  request_id: "req-9a7f",
  tenant: "cust-712",
  model_id: "gpt-large-v1",
  output: "...",
  debug.context: "tenant:cust-319 prompt_id: p-3f2e..."
}
```

IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for oncall @Maya due to alert 'vpc-response-mismatch' (severity P1). Link to alert: https://mon.redwood/alerts/2379998888. PagerDuty incident: PD-5821.

PagerDuty: Assigned to Maya. Escalation level: 1.

Maya (oncall): on it. looking at ingress logs and route audit now. @Julian @Tim please standby. Simon — thanks for flagging. can you confirm you still have the original response body? any more examples?

Simon (Customer): I saved the full body and timestamps. next one at 09:18:11Z. happy to DM. not sending full payload in thread.

Julian (infra): pulling route tables and pool allocations for prod-712. running a quick prefix-scan against dedicated pool routing.

Tim (eng-runtime): replicating locally — running a KV cache read-only sweep for cust-712 for last 15m. possible cross-read from prefix shadowing.

Elisa (security): please snapshot evidence and isolate storage/kv reads. if there is any chance of cross-tenant exposure we need a containment plan first. do NOT delete logs until we capture them.

Maya (oncall): timeline so far: 09:12 initial resp, 09:18 second. incidentbot alert at 09:19, page at 09:20. I'm going to re-route all prod-712 requests to a cold pool to stop further KVCACHE hits while we triage. will post command.

Maya (oncall): executing hotfix: 
```bash
# temporary failover to isolation pool
rdwctl route set --tenant cust-712 --pool isolation-pool-01 --reason "live mitigation: suspected cross-tenant read"
```

Maya (oncall): applied. returning 202 response for new incoming requests while we confirm. @Lee please prep a customer-facing note — short acknowledgement + we are investigating and temporarily routing to isolated pool.

Lee (acct): drafting. ETA 10m. cc @Simon (Customer) for review.

Julian (infra): evidence snapshotting: 
```bash
# collect routing tables and netns for impacted nodes
ssh node-gpu-17 "sudo ip netns exec rdw-serving cat /proc/net/route > /tmp/rt-cust-712 && sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/pkt-capture.pcap -i eth0 "host 10.3.72.15" " 
```
Collecting pod attachments and pool assignments now.

Tim (eng-runtime): found KV read sequence where key-prefix collision might happen: some older pool reservation accidentally used a global prefix map for short-lived canaries. grabbing logs: 
```
kubectl -n redwood logs pod/serving-abc123 --since=20m | grep "kv_read" | grep "cust-712" -n
```
Result shows kv_read entries with neighbor prefixes around the same timestamp. attaching sanitized snippet to thread DM.

Elisa (security): good. capture full request/response headers and the X-Redwood-Tenant header values. also capture KV shard ids for the read ops. we need to know if any payload was actually served from the other tenant's cache.

Maya (oncall): I am going to put an eviction hold on the suspected pool instance to prevent new allocations and schedule a live scrub. command: 
```bash
rdwctl pool freeze --pool p-dedicated-47 --reason "suspected prefix shadowing"
rdwctl pool scrub --pool p-dedicated-47 --mode read-only --until 09:30
```

Maya (oncall): freeze applied. scrub in progress. scrub logs show ~3 hits that match cust-319 prefixes during the window.

Julian (infra): routing audit shows an ACL rule that briefly allowed a legacy prefix 10.120.0.0/16 to be treated as shared for edge-caching. it was part of a migration script on 2026-03-10 and never fully rolled back. I'm pulling the change: 
```diff
- route-map allow edge-cache 10.120.0.0/16 -> shared
+ route-map deny edge-cache 10.120.0.0/16 -> per-tenant
```
This would explain the observed shadow reads.

Tim (eng-runtime): confirming: the runtime used shared prefix map for caching lookups if prefix len < 24. Migration accidentally added cust-319 to the shared prefix. That means keys with that short prefix could end up in the same shard.

Elisa (security): immediate actions recommended:
- keep pool frozen until we can re-key the KV shards for the window
- run forensic integrity on any potentially affected keys
- produce a minimal impact statement for legal/compliance

Maya (oncall): Agreed. next steps I'm executing now: 1) keep freeze, 2) roll back migration change from 03/10, 3) reassign cust-712 to fresh pool with cleared prefixes, 4) rotate shard keys for the affected KV range, 5) prep customer comms with Lee.

Maya (oncall): executing rollback: 
```bash
git revert -m 1 3f2e9b1 -- path=infra/route-maps/migration-20260310.conf
infractl deploy --staging-checks --target infra-edge-1
```
Deploy triggered. will monitor tail of deploy logs.

Lee (acct): drafted customer note: 
"Hi Simon — we saw anomalous routing in your VPC that may have returned cached fragments from a different tenant. We have temporarily routed your traffic to an isolated pool and are performing a forensic investigation. No confirmed exposure of PII at this time. We will provide an update within 2 hours. — Lee, Redwood"

Simon (Customer): thanks. appreciate the quick containment. will wait for update. can you confirm if any stored files were exposed? we have sensitive embeddings stored.

Elisa (security): we will check embedding shard access logs. initial evidence suggests small textual fragments only, no full document retrievals. but we must treat as potential exposure until proven otherwise.

Tim (eng-runtime): shard key rotation job queued: 
```bash
kvctl rotate-keys --shard-range 10.120.0.0/16 --force --window 09:25-09:45
```
Will monitor progress and report back.

Julian (infra): deploy rollback completed at 09:26. ACLs reverted. confirmed 0 rules allowing the legacy shared prefix remain.

Maya (oncall): reassigned cust-712 to isolation pool at 09:27 and kept p-dedicated-47 frozen. kv key rotation started. scrubbing evidence continues.

Elisa (security): retrieving list of keys and potential recipients. creating internal incident artifact for compliance with link: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/2379998888-forensics

Lee (acct): sending initial customer note now. Simon, I cc'ed you.

Simon (Customer): got it. thank you. ping me if you need logs from our side.

Maya (oncall): interim update (09:34): containment complete, no new cross-tenant hits since failover. rotation job reports 0 failed shards. forensic team will finish evidence pack in ~45m. escalation to legal/compliance if needed.

IncidentBot: Incident PD-5821 updated: status=investigating -> contained. severity remains P1 until full forensics complete.

Elisa (security): action items for postmortem:
- root cause: migration left legacy prefix in shared prefix map causing cache key collisions for short prefixes
- short-term fix: stricter prefix validation in migration tooling, abort-deploy checks for shared-prefix introduces
- long-term: per-tenant prefix hashing and stronger KV namespace separation + integration tests

Tim (eng-runtime): will open PR for runtime guard: reject shared-prefix map entries with prefix length <24 unless explicit opt-in.

Maya (oncall): handing off to daytime SRE for follow-up: @Julian please own the rollback verification and postmortem. @Elisa you own forensics and compliance notes. @Tim follow runtime patch. @Lee customer comms. I'll update PD and mark handoff at 09:45.

Julian (infra): acknowledged. taking ownership. will post timeline + mitigation steps in the postmortem thread.

Maya (oncall): closing live pager handoff. last update 09:45.

PagerDuty: PD-5821 status: assigned -> acknowledged -> delegated to JulIan at 09:45.

Simon (Customer): thanks everyone. appreciate the transparency.
